title: Understanding Cross-Validation
text: Cross-validation is a technique used to assess the performance of a model by dividing the data into multiple subsets. Each subset is used as a test set while the remaining data is used for training. This process is repeated multiple times, and the results are averaged to provide a more accurate estimate of the model's performance.

title: Choosing the Best Lambda
text: The goal is to choose the lambda value that minimizes the cross-validation error. Look at the root-mean square error for each lambda and select the one with the lowest error.

title: Analyzing the Errors
text:
Suppose the root-mean square errors for each lambda are as follows:
- $$lambda=0.001$$: $$0.15$$
- $$lambda=0.01$$: $$0.12$$
- $$lambda=0.1$$: $$0.14$$
- $$lambda=1$$: $$0.18$$
- $$lambda=10$$: $$0.20$$
Which lambda has the lowest error?
